:::{#exm-flat-point-critical}
#### The flat points of a cubic, and a critical point that is not flat

For $f(w) = w^3 - 3w$, the derivative is $f'(w) = 3w^2 - 3$.
The code differentiates $f$ with `D()` and evaluates $f'$ at several points.
For $g(w) = \abs{w}$, it computes the difference quotients at $0$ from both sides.

```{r}
#| label: flat-point-critical
#| code-fold: false
f_prime <- D(quote(w^3 - 3 * w), "w")
points <- c(-2, -1, 0, 1, 2)
derivs <- data.frame(w = points, f_prime = eval(f_prime, list(w = points)))
derivs
flat <- derivs$w[derivs$f_prime == 0]

h <- c(-1e-3, 1e-3)
quotients <- abs(h) / h
quotients
```

The derivative is $0$ at `{r} sum(derivs$f_prime == 0)` of the `{r} nrow(derivs)` points,
namely $w = `{r} flat[1]`$ and $w = `{r} flat[2]`$.
These are flat points of $f$, so by @thm-flat-point-critical they are critical points.
The difference quotients of $g$ at $0$ are `{r} quotients[1]` from the left and `{r} quotients[2]` from the right,
so $g$ has no derivative at $0$.
Thus $0$ is a critical point of $g$ (@def-critical-point), but not a flat point.

:::
